label: Plunderphonics named
detail: John Oswald coins the word, in an essay, for music made openly from other recordings.

label: 'Fish Market' riddim
detail: Steely & Clevie cut the Jamaican riddim that their lawsuit names as the source of reggaeton's dembow pattern.

label: 'Trip hop' in print
detail: Mixmag's Andy Pemberton uses the term for DJ Shadow's 'In/Flux'; Portishead's 'Dummy' follows later in the year.

label: 'Since I Left You'
detail: The Avalanches release their sample collage in Australia; it is usually put at more than 3,500 samples, and the 2001 international editions drop the ones that could not be cleared.

label: WhoSampled launches
detail: The user-submitted sample database goes live from London late in the year.

label: J Dilla's MPC goes to the Smithsonian
detail: Maureen Yancey donates her son's MPC and custom Moog to the National Museum of African American History and Culture.

label: Sample drill gets a name in print
detail: Complex writes up New York drill built on recognizable R&B and pop samples.

label: 'Heart on My Sleeve' removed
detail: The AI voice-clone track imitating Drake and The Weeknd is pulled from streaming services after 629,439 Spotify streams.

label: An AI-generated sample is cleared
detail: Complex reports that 'U My Everything' samples the Udio-generated 'BBL Drizzy', cleared by licensing only the human-written publishing.

label: Universal settles with Udio
detail: The first of three label settlements with AI music generators, with licenses and a joint platform planned for 2026.

label: Spotify buys WhoSampled
detail: Price undisclosed; the database then lists 1.2 million songs and 622,000 samples (company figures).

label: Warner settles with Suno
detail: Terms private; Suno agrees to launch licensed models and retire its current ones.

label: GEMA v. Suno
detail: Munich Regional Court I rules largely for the German authors' society over six compositions; Suno appeals and the judgment is not final.

label: Dembow ruling
detail: In Browne v. Clark the judge grants the defendants summary judgment on the selection-and-arrangement theory; other claims continue.

label: Universal and Sony sue Suno again
detail: A second suit in Massachusetts federal court covers 60,202 recordings and Suno's v6 models, after a judge declined to add them to the 2024 case.
